Hi Phil,

I am using the mirtCAT package to simulate an adaptive item selection procedure from a 2-factor between-item MIRT model. I learned the multi-unidimensional example you provided to select 5 items for each domain separately. I also add the MH exposure control and the content balancing to the item selection procedure, but I get an error message: content designs are not supported for seq criteria.
If I delete the content design commands, the codes would work well. Do you know the right way to set the content constraints in my case? I paste part of my codes below for your reference. Your help would be greatly appreciated!

#item bank is simulated from a between-item 2pl
nitems=dim(bank)[1]
A=rowSums(bank[,c(1:2)],na.rm=T)

mo <- generate.mirt_object(bank, itemtype='2PL')
#SH: create an exposure control list
SH <- rep(1, nitems)
SH <- ifelse(A > 1.5, 0.9, SH)
SH <- ifelse(A > 2, 0.6, SH)
SH <- ifelse(A > 2.5, 0.3, SH)

customNextItem <- function(design, person, test){
  block1 <- 1:(nitems/2)
  block2 <- (nitems/2+1):nitems
  total_answered <- sum(!is.na <http://is.na>(extract.mirtCAT(person, 'items_answered')))
  if(total_answered < 5){ #first 5 items block1
    block <- block1
  } else if(total_answered < 10){ #next 10 block2
    block <- block2
  } else return(NA) # terminate when both item blocks have 5 items answered
  ret <- findNextItem(person=person, design=design, test=test,
                      subset=block, criteria = 'KL')
  ret
}
content <- rep(rep(paste("f", 1:5, sep = ""), c(27,21,17,19,35)),2)
content_prop=c("f1" = 0.2, "f2" = 0.15,"f3"=0.2,"f4"=0.15,
               "f5"=0.3)
design <- list(customNextItem=customNextItem,max_items = 10,exposure = SH,
               content = content,
               content_prop = content_prop)
#simulate response pattern
resp <- generate_pattern(mo, as.matrix(theta[cols.num]))
result <- mirtCAT(mo = mo, local_pattern = resp, start_item = "KL",
                    design = design)

Thanks,
Jiaying

messages.body_plain:
Hello. I realized that the M2 function provides different outputs depending on item type. More specifically, the residual matrices differ.

If I use itemtype = "gpcm" or itemtype = "grm", I got all fit indices including SRMSR. If I use itemtype = "gpcmIRT", SRMSR is not returned.

I tried to find the reason, and I realized that residual matrices differ. With itemtype = "gpcm" and M2(..., residmat = T), M2 function returns squared matrix with residuals in lower triangle. If the same is repeated with itemtype = "gpcmIRT", M2 function provides a list of objects
> ls(fit_config)
[1] "delta"   "e"       "estpars" "p"       "SRMSR"   "Xi2"
where SRMSR object is NULL.

I wonder if this is an error or if SRMSR cannot be computed with gpcmIRT parameterization (which does not make sense to me). Can I get SRMSR with gpcmIRT parameterization? The reason for that parameterization is invariance testing, where I want to test threshold and scalar invariance levels separately (constraining b parameters while releasing c parameter in the second group).

Hi Phil,

I really love the mirtCAT package! Thank you so much for the work. I find even if I set the same seed value before the mirtCAT function, the generating object is still different. In this case, how can I replicate the results? I use the example codes you shared in the article and make slight changes. Do you have anything in your mind?

Best,
Jiaying

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

### Appendix B simulation
library("mirtCAT")
library("plyr")
library("mvtnorm")
library("parallel")
nitems <- 360
N <- 500
cl <- makeCluster(detectCores())
set.seed(123)
a <- matrix(c(rlnorm(nitems, 0.2, 0.3), rlnorm(nitems/3, -1, 0.2), numeric(nitems),
  rlnorm(nitems/3, -1, 0.2), numeric(nitems), rlnorm(nitems/3, -1, 0.2)), nitems,
  4)
d <- data.frame(d = rnorm(nitems/2))
g <- c(rep(0.2, nitems/2), rep(NA, nitems/2))
u <- c(rep(0.95, nitems/2), rep(NA, nitems/2))
ds <- data.frame(matrix(rnorm(nitems * 2, 0, 2), nitems/2, 4))
ints <- rbind.fill(d, ds)

pars <- data.frame(a, g, u, ints)
colnames(pars) <- c(paste0("a", 1:4), "g", "u", "d", paste0("d", 1:4))
itemtype <- c(rep("4PL", nitems/2), rep("gpcm", nitems/2))
SH <- rep(1, nitems)
SH <- ifelse(a[, 1] > 1, 0.9, SH)
SH <- ifelse(a[, 1] > 2, 0.6, SH)
SH <- ifelse(a[, 1] > 2.5, 0.3, SH)
content <- rep(c("4PL", "gpcm"), each = nitems/2)
content_prop <- c(`4PL` = 0.7, gpcm = 0.3)

               max_items = 50, exposure = SH, content = content, content_prop = content_prop)
set.seed(233)
mo <- generate.mirt_object(pars, itemtype)
Theta <- rmvnorm(N, sigma = diag(4))
resp <- generate_pattern(mo, Theta)
result <- mirtCAT(mo = mo, local_pattern = resp, start_item = "KL", criteria = "KL",
  design = design, cl = cl)

set.seed(233)
mo <- generate.mirt_object(pars, itemtype)
Theta <- rmvnorm(N, sigma = diag(4))
resp <- generate_pattern(mo, Theta)
result2 <- mirtCAT(mo = mo, local_pattern = resp, start_item = "KL", criteria = "KL",
                  design = design, cl = cl)
realresp<-do.call(rbind,lapply(result,function(x) x$scored_responses))
realresp2<-do.call(rbind,lapply(result2,function(x) x$scored_responses))

#different outputs
all.equal(result, result,2)
all.equal(realresp, realresp2)

messages.body_plain:
Hello Dr. Chalmers,

I was working on DIF with 4 groups and was seeing some unexpected results. I suspected that the Wald test was not generating the correct L matrix for 4 groups. I created a minimally reproducible example with 4 groups, 5 items, DIF on item 5 using the Rasch model. Given the degree of DIF injected into item 5 for group 4 I would expect significant results. Perhaps I did something incorrectly in the way I am specifying the model? Would you take a look?

nitem = 5

n.g1 = 2000
n.g2 = 1000
n.g3 = 1000
n.g4 = 1000

groups = c(rep('g1', n.g1), rep('g2', n.g2), rep('g3', n.g3), rep('g4', n.g4))

a <- rep(1, nitem)
d1 <- d2 <- d3 <- d4 <- matrix(rnorm(nitem,0,.7),ncol=1)
d4[5, ] <- d1[5, ] + 1 # here is the DIF

item.type <- rep('dich', nitem)

# Generate data
dat1 <- simdata(a, d1, n.g1, item.type)
dat2 <- simdata(a, d2, n.g2, item.type)
dat3 <- simdata(a, d3, n.g3, item.type)
dat4 <- simdata(a, d4, n.g4, item.type)

dat <- rbind(dat1,dat2,dat3,dat4)

test.model <- mirt(dat,1,'Rasch')

anchor.set <- colnames(dat)[1:4]

res.model <- multipleGroup(dat, 1,
                           group = groups,
                           itemtype = "Rasch",
                           invariance = c("free_var", "free_mean", anchor.set),
                           SE = T)

res.dif <- DIF(res.model,c('d'), Wald = T, items2test = 5)

# Results:
# > res.dif

messages.body_plain:
This is generally to be expected given that estimation is quite sensitive to parameterization given only a 1 × 10-4 convergence criteria in the EM. You could lower the TOL argument until they agree better, but there's no guarantee that they will converge to each other exactly without very large sample sizes (this is why parameterization can be tricky, and why the package generally prefers the slope-intercept versions for their improved stability). Here's a script worth experimenting with to see this:

library(mirt)
a <- matrix(rlnorm(20,.2,.3))
diffs <- t(apply(matrix(runif(20*4, .3, 1), 20), 1, cumsum))
diffs <- -(diffs - rowMeans(diffs))
d <- diffs + rnorm(20)

dat <- simdata(a, d, 5000, itemtype = 'graded') # change the sample size/TOL criteria

mod <- mirt(dat, 1, 'gpcm')
mod2 <- mirt(dat, 1, 'gpcmIRT', TOL=1e-6)

coef(mod, IRTpars=TRUE, simplify=TRUE)$items
coef(mod2, simplify=TRUE)$items

M2(mod)
M2(mod2)

messages.subject: Re: CFA results do not fit with EFA results
messages.subject_clean: CFA results do not fit with EFA results
messages.body_plain:
This can happen because EFA models have numerous loadings on their minor factors, which has the effect of improving the fit statistics due to chance capitalization + overfitting. As these factors all have only three loadings they are generally weakly defined, and it's likely the case there is more complex relationships going on in the response data (cross-loadings, residual covariation, higher-order structures, etc). I don't believe I can offer advice on improving the fit as this requires much theoretical consideration given the test content and causal theory connecting the constructs to the items.

Phil

My intention is to use the SH to control item exposure but still administer items adaptively by using the "KL" algorithm. The reason I create the CustomNextItem function is to make sure each examinee receives the same number of items for each domain.

After I posted my question, I tried an alternative way to deal with the content balancing issue: I set the content proportion as a test property and generate a constraint funciton. Please let me know whether this seting also makes sense.

#SH: create an exposure control list
SH <- rep(1, nitems)

SH <- ifelse(a1 > 2, 0.6, SH)

  content=c(rep(paste("f", 1:5, sep = ""), c(27,21,17,19,35)),rep(paste("g", 1:5, sep = ""), c(27,21,17,19,35)))
                             )
# constraint generating function
constr_fun <- function(person, test, design){
  mo <- extract.mirtCAT(test, 'mo')
  nitems <- extract.mirt(mo, 'nitems')
  tp <- extract.mirtCAT(design, 'test_properties')

  lhs <- matrix(0, 12, nitems)
  lhs[1,] <- 1
  lhs[2,tp$stimuli == 'T1'] <- 1
  lhs[2,tp$stimuli == 'T2'] <- -1
  lhs[3,tp$content == 'f1'] <- 1
  lhs[4, tp$content == 'f2'] <- 1
  lhs[5, tp$content == 'f3'] <- 1
  lhs[6, tp$content == 'f4'] <- 1
  lhs[7, tp$content == 'f5'] <- 1
  lhs[8, tp$content == 'g1'] <- 1
  lhs[9, tp$content == 'g2'] <- 1
  lhs[10, tp$content == 'g3'] <- 1
  lhs[11, tp$content == 'g4'] <- 1
  lhs[12, tp$content == 'g5'] <- 1

  # relationship direction
  dirs <- c("==", "==", '<=', '<=', '<=', '<=', '<=','<=','<=','<=','<=','<=')

  #right hand side
  rhs <- c(10, 0, 1, 1, 1,1,2, 1, 1, 1,1,2)

  #all together
  constraints <- data.frame(lhs, dirs, rhs)
  constraints
}
# next item selection function
customNextItem <- function(person, design, test){
  objective <- computeCriteria(person=person, design=design, test=test,
                               criteria = 'KL')
  item <- findNextItem(person=person, design=design, test=test,
                       objective=objective)
  item
}
design <- list(exposure = SH,
               customNextItem=customNextItem,
               constr_fun=constr_fun,
               test_properties=test_properties,
               min_SEM=0)

Thanks, all variants in DIF with more than two groups should be patched now on the dev. When 3 or more groups are specified joint tests for DIF are performed, however in situations where post-hoc DIF testing is to be investigated there is now a groups2test input to isolate the individual grouping variable combinations (e.g., groups2test = c('g1', 'g2')). Phil
